workflows.label: Assign a saved projectile to your player's weapon
workflows.prerequisites: An open project with a Player Start, a saved weapon selected in STARTING EQUIPMENT, a launch-capable action and a saved projectile. If you only have a draft projectile, finish **SAVE AS NEW** first. This guide does not create the Player Start or weapon.
steps: Select **Player Start** in **Scene Hierarchy**, then open **STARTING EQUIPMENT** → **WEAPON FIRING**.
Choose **Weapon hand** (Primary hand or Off hand) and the appropriate **Launch on** action. Use the action configured for your weapon; do not assume every bow uses Release charged action.
Set **Fire mode** to **Projectile / travelling** and select your saved projectile in the projectile dropdown.
Choose your weapon's defined **Spawn point**. The tested bow uses Bow_Nock; your point may have a different name.
Check **Fire at**: **Animation start** fires immediately; **After a delay** waits for the configured time. Keep your existing verified timing when only replacing the projectile.
Click **APPLY TO THIS PLAYER**, then **Ctrl+S** to save the level.
workflows.follow_up: Use **PLAY** to launch Test Level and fire using your configured weapon input. Reopen the saved scene and check that the projectile, spawn point and timing remain selected.

If the panel says Weapon changed, reopen Weapon firing before applying.

If the shot starts in the wrong place or at the wrong time, check Spawn point and Fire at.

workflows.label: Create a new travelling projectile
workflows.prerequisites: An open Renegade project with a Player Start and a weapon/equipment setup. If you have not created these yet, ask for the Player Start or starting-equipment walkthrough first.
steps: Select **Player Start** in the **Scene Hierarchy** (usually under **Characters**).
Open **STARTING EQUIPMENT** → **WEAPON FIRING**. Choose the appropriate weapon hand and launch action.
Set **Fire mode** to **Projectile / travelling**, then click **NEW**.
**NEW** starts with the **Bullet** preset. Keep Bullet or choose **Arrow**, **Bolt**, **Thrown projectile** or **Spell projectile**, then give it a name.
Configure speed, gravity, damage and any visible model. For example, the **Arrow** preset starts at **45 m/s** and **Gravity 1**; **Stick** needs a visible model.
Click **SAVE AS NEW** to create a reusable projectile asset.
workflows.follow_up: To actually fire it, select the saved projectile in **Weapon firing**, choose its **Spawn point** and launch timing, click **APPLY TO THIS PLAYER**, save the level (**Ctrl+S**) and test with **PLAY**. Saving the projectile alone does not equip it.

workflows.label: Place a Player Start
workflows.prerequisites: An open project and level. For movement testing, provide a floor with working collision. New levels have no automatically placed Player Start.
steps: Open the **Asset Browser** and browse to **Content/Player**.
Choose **Basic Player Start**, or an existing saved player prefab in this project.
Drag the preset into the scene viewport onto the intended spawn surface. The editor selects the placed player and shows its capsule.
Use the transform gizmo to position the capsule and set its facing. Keep the spawn clear of obstacles.
Check the selected Player Start's **Inspector** for its controller and camera settings.
Save the level with **Ctrl+S**.
workflows.follow_up: Use **PLAY** to start Test Level and check spawn position, facing and movement. Reopen the saved scene to check persistence.
workflows.expected_result: One Player Start is placed in the level. A Basic Player Start supplies controller defaults; it does not create a weapon or arms setup.
troubleshooting: If placement says PLAYER ALREADY PLACED, select the existing Player Start. Change its prefab in the Inspector, or delete it before deliberately placing a replacement.
If the player falls or starts inside geometry, check floor collision and move the spawn clear of obstacles.
If Content/Player is missing, check that a project is open and refresh the Asset Browser; the current browser scan ensures the Basic preset.
Do not look for Player Start in the Add menu; the current placement workflow uses Content/Player.

workflows.label: Save a reusable Player Prefab
workflows.prerequisites: An open project and an existing Player Start configured with the settings you want to reuse. This saves player defaults; it does not create missing arms or equipment assets.
steps: Select the existing **Player Start** in **Scene Hierarchy**.
Check its controller, camera, arms and starting-equipment settings in the **Inspector**. The prefab captures the player's current settings.
Click **SAVE AS PLAYER PREFAB**. The saved prefab takes its display name from the Player Start's name and appears under **Content/Player**.
Save the level with **Ctrl+S** to retain this Player Start's prefab assignment.
workflows.follow_up: In another level in the same project, drag the saved prefab from Content/Player into the viewport. If a Player Start already exists there, choose the prefab in its Inspector instead.
workflows.expected_result: A new reusable Player Prefab is saved and assigned. Each save creates a separate prefab; it does not overwrite a shared prefab or update every placed player.
troubleshooting: If the controls are missing, select the Player Start rather than a weapon or NPC.
If saving reports an error, use the displayed error to check referenced assets; do not assume the save succeeded.
If the prefab cannot be placed, check whether that level already has a Player Start.
Spawn position and facing remain specific to each level; they are not shared prefab defaults.

workflows.label: Restore assigned Player Prefab defaults
workflows.prerequisites: Select a Player Start with an assigned prefab and local changes you intend to discard. RESET TO PREFAB restores its assigned defaults, so review those changes first.
steps: Select **Player Start** and open its **Inspector**.
Check the prefab status. **PREFAB // LOCAL OVERRIDES** means the current settings differ from its assigned defaults.
Click **RESET TO PREFAB** to restore that assigned baseline.
Check the restored settings, then save the level with **Ctrl+S** if you want to retain them.
workflows.follow_up: Use Undo if the reset was unintended. Test movement and any equipped setup with PLAY after saving.
workflows.expected_result: Local setting overrides return to the assigned prefab defaults. The level's spawn position and facing remain unchanged.
troubleshooting: If RESET TO PREFAB is unavailable, there may be no assigned baseline or no local overrides.
**CUSTOM PLAYER // NO PREFAB** means there is no assigned prefab to reset to. Choose an appropriate saved prefab in the Inspector first if that is your intention.
This restores the assigned baseline; it does not restart Test Level or respawn the player.
Saving a new prefab elsewhere does not automatically replace this level's assigned defaults.

workflows.label: Create equipment from a saved arms assembly
workflows.prerequisites: An open project with a Player Start whose arms reference is already a saved first-person assembly. Importing loose arms/weapon models is not enough. The saved assembly must contain the actions you want; this panel does not invent missing animations.
steps: Select **Player Start** in **Scene Hierarchy** and open **STARTING EQUIPMENT** in its **Inspector**.
Enter a readable item name in **New item**.

Choose **Hand use** to match the item: **PrimaryOnly**, **OffHandOnly**, **EitherHand**, **TwoHanded** or **PrimaryWithSupport**. The panel initially selects TwoHanded; change it when your setup requires a different policy.
Click **CREATE FROM ASSEMBLY**. This uses the Player Start's assigned saved assembly.
After the Created confirmation, select the new item in **Primary hand** or **Off hand**, as permitted by its Hand use.
For **TwoHanded** or **PrimaryWithSupport** in Primary hand, leave **Off hand** as **NONE**. Then click **APPLY LOADOUT**.
Save the level with **Ctrl+S**.
workflows.follow_up: Use **PLAY** to check your existing equipment actions. If you want it to launch a projectile, use **WEAPON FIRING** and configure a supported launch action separately.
workflows.expected_result: A new equipment definition exists and the selected loadout is applied. CREATE FROM ASSEMBLY alone does not equip the item or configure projectile firing.
troubleshooting: If creation fails, check that the assigned arms reference is a saved first-person assembly and read the displayed EQUIPMENT error.
If an action is missing, check the saved assembly's matching action tracks; this panel does not create or retarget clips.
If your new item is absent from a hand selector, check its Hand use policy.
If the loadout is rejected, remove an incompatible off-hand item or choose equipment with compatible hand policies.

workflows.label: Assign the player's starting equipment
workflows.prerequisites: An open project, a Player Start and saved equipment definitions in this project. If you only have a saved first-person assembly, use CREATE FROM ASSEMBLY to create an equipment definition first.
steps: Select **Player Start** in **Scene Hierarchy**, then open **STARTING EQUIPMENT** in the **Inspector**.
Choose a compatible saved item in **Primary hand**. Select **NONE** if you intend to leave that slot empty.
Choose a compatible item in **Off hand**, or **NONE**. **TwoHanded** and **PrimaryWithSupport** primary items reserve both hands, so leave Off hand empty for those.
Click **APPLY LOADOUT** and check that the panel confirms the loadout was applied.
Save the level with **Ctrl+S**.
workflows.follow_up: Use **PLAY** to test the configured equipment. Reopen the saved scene and check both hand selections. To reuse these defaults later, save a Player Prefab.
workflows.expected_result: The selected Player Start uses the chosen saved loadout. Editing dropdowns alone does not commit the assignment; APPLY LOADOUT and saving the level are separate actions.
troubleshooting: If an item is missing, check it was saved as an equipment definition in this project; a loose model is not an equipment item.
If a slot says **MISSING / INCOMPATIBLE**, choose a valid saved item or NONE and read any LOADOUT error.
Off hand accepts **OffHandOnly** or **EitherHand** items. A two-handed primary item cannot be combined with an off-hand item.
Use Undo if you applied the wrong loadout. Projectile launch settings are a separate WEAPON FIRING task.

workflows.label: Import and place a static model
native_checks: Generated static GLB native proof passed preview, commit, placement, Undo/Redo and scene save/reopen
Generated textured static FBX native proof passed texture rejection, retained reimport and placement/save/reopen
workflows.prerequisites: An open Renegade project and a static **GLB or FBX** model with its required textures available. This guide covers static objects; rigged characters and external animations use separate workflows. The current native picker offers GLB/FBX.
steps: Open **ADD** → **IMPORT MODEL...**, then select your GLB or FBX file.
Wait for the rendered preview. Check the model and textures; use **ROTATE LEFT** or **ROTATE RIGHT** to inspect it. Preview rotation does not change the imported asset.
Enter a readable **Asset name**.
Choose **Folder**, or type a project-relative folder in **Import to**, such as **Content/Models/Props**. A valid new Content folder is created during import. Do not enter a Windows absolute path.
For an ordinary prop, leave **Asset role** as **General model**. Optional comma-separated **Tags** help searching; they do not choose the folder or turn a model into equipment.
Click **IMPORT ASSET** when the preview is ready. Check the registered-asset confirmation and the revealed **Asset Browser** card.
Drag that imported card into the scene viewport, position it with the gizmo, then save the level with **Ctrl+S**.
workflows.follow_up: Reopen the saved scene and check the placed model. Importing creates a reusable asset; placing it and saving the scene are separate steps.
workflows.expected_result: The model is registered in your chosen Content folder and its placed instance is retained in the saved level. This does not automatically add collision, NPC behaviour or weapon gameplay.
troubleshooting: If IMPORT ASSET is disabled, wait for the preview; if conversion fails, read the reported error rather than assuming an asset was saved.
For a textured FBX, keep required images in the exported source folder tree with valid relative references; missing or changed textures can block import.
A GLB filename does not guarantee embedded textures. External image references are not supported by this import path; export a self-contained GLB.
If the status says COMMITTED; REVEAL FAILED, browse the chosen Content folder. Do not import again merely because the card was not revealed.
An existing name/destination can be rejected to protect an asset. Check the error and choose a distinct name instead of overwriting files manually.
If the importer detects a rigged character, stop and use the Character workflow instead; this static guide does not cover animation assignment.
